checksums.name: self_complement_wordsum_candidate
checksums.formula_detail: Decompiled from FUN_0807eebc/FUN_0807f078: zero word0, set word1=0xFFFFFFFF, sum all 32 u32 words (little-endian, plain 32-bit wraparound add, no carry-out) of a 128-byte buffer, store sum at word0 and ~sum at word1. Self-checking invariant: word1 must equal ~word0, and re-summing all 32 stored words must reproduce word0. PROVEN NOT TO MATCH the actual bytes at 0x7040 in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav (word0=0x990a011f, word1=0x545366f5, ~word0=0x66f5fee0 != word1).

io_driver_functions.notes: Hardware wait-state register read-modify-write (bits forced to 3) then a copy loop and tail-call into an unresolved function; plausible WAITCNT-class setup before SRAM access.

Raw byte-copy loop (*dst++ = *src++) after the same register fixup. Called with destination literal 0xe000000 (SRAM base) and size 0x8000 (full 32KB) from FUN_08000c60 - the primary full-save-flush driver.
Same structural shape as 0x08004c54 but with distinct globals; used as the read-back/verify half of the write-verify-retry wrapper.
Write (08004c54) then verify (08004cc4), retry up to 3 times. Also reused for non-save DMA/graphics buffer copies elsewhere in the binary - not save-exclusive.
Enqueues a generic DMA job then calls FUN_08004c54(src, 0xe000000, 0x8000) - flushes the entire 32,768-byte RAM save mirror to SRAM.

Two FUN_08004d28 calls of size 0x80 (128 bytes) each, matching the exact size of the 0x7040-0x70BF block observed in the .sav files. Likely the 128-byte-slot I/O routine, though its target buffer could not be statically resolved to 0x7040.
Two FUN_08004bf0 calls (sizes 0x100 and 0x80). Only invoked from FUN_0807ef28 on a first-run flag; plausible one-time boot init read.

Serializes fixed/copied bytes into a 128-byte buffer and computes the self-complement word-sum checksum described above, then calls 0x08000c98 to flush. Proven in SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md Section 4.3 not to match the actual 0x7040 block bytes.

Validates one of 3 candidate 128-byte slots (param 0/1/2), recomputing the same word-sum and returning a 3-bit failure mask (sum mismatch / 20-byte sub-block mismatch / complement mismatch). No callers resolved in the static trace.

Top-level save-slot dispatcher: validates 3 redundant candidate slots via 0x0807f078(0|1|2), then triggers repair (0x08000c60 full flush + 0x0807eebc re-serialize) if any slot was invalid. No callers resolved (reached via unrecovered jump table).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Save-subsystem umbrella entry point; calls the slot dispatcher among 3 other subsystem calls (0807fb84, 080800f4, 08080264) that do not appear save-related (DMA sizes 0x1200 consistent with graphics/OBJ transfers).
ram_fields_updated: unresolved IWRAM/EWRAM slot-candidate buffers (_DAT_0807ef1c, puRam0807f040-family globals)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced via ghidra/callgraph.json callees list for 0x0807eea4 and ghidra/decompiled.c bodies for each listed function; confirmed call arguments/sizes by reading each decompiled function body directly.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Full 32KB SRAM flush path taken when the slot dispatcher decides a full rewrite is needed.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced via callgraph.json callees for 0807ef28 and 08000c60, cross-checked against the literal 0x8000/0xe000000 arguments visible in ghidra/decompiled.c.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the language-index hypothesis is correct, in-game text language changes on next load; if not, no observable change and the engine may simply overwrite the value verbatim on next save.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: zero, then randomize the 6 opaque bytes preceding the STARTKEYLANGUAGE tag
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is a guarded length/counter field, the game should detect corruption and re-initialize or skip the block; if inert, no observable effect.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: fill the entire 128-byte block with 0xFF, restoring it to the cap-00 blank appearance
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests whether the game tolerates loss of this block (falls back to default language) or treats it as fatal; also probes whether this offset is one of the 3 redundant candidate slots validated by FUN_0807ef28/FUN_0807f078.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip header 'VF01' tag to 'VF00' at offset 0x0000 only, leaving the 0x7100 mirror intact
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If a selection/fallback rule between the two header copies exists, the game should still boot using the intact 0x7100 copy and potentially repair the corrupted one on next save; if not, this is the first evidence the two copies are never cross-validated at runtime.

open_questions: Does FUN_0807ef28's 3-way redundant checksum/slot-repair scheme (FUN_0807f078/FUN_0807eebc) protect the 0x7040-0x70BF block observed in these samples, or an entirely different, not-yet-populated SRAM offset? The one's-complement self-check invariant fails against the actual bytes at 0x7040, so this is unresolved.
What writer produces the STARTKEYLANGUAGE/ENDKEY_LANGUAGE_ tag block, since it lies outside the 88-function/5-seed Ghidra trace set entirely?
Is the opaque 4-byte header prefix (0xBE 0xD7 0xA9 0xB9) a fixed build-time constant, or does it vary across cartridge instances/other release builds? Only one cartridge instance was sampled here.

Is the 0x02 byte between the STARTKEYLANGUAGE/ENDKEY_LANGUAGE_ tags actually a language selector, or merely a coincidentally-named debug variable? Requires a second non-blank sample with a different selected language to confirm.
Does a selection/fallback rule exist between the two byte-identical header copies at 0x0000 and 0x7100, or are they simply always kept in sync and never independently validated at runtime?

Are there additional save fields entirely outside the 3 active ranges identified here (i.e. further into the game, more SRAM regions would become non-blank)? Only 2 early sequential checkpoint captures were available for this release key.
